questions.q: A contract promises revenue "on a recurring basis" rather than from a single sale. Which description best preserves this distinction?
options: Revenue expected to arise repeatedly over the relevant periods.
Revenue necessarily received entirely in cash at the start of the contract.
Revenue earned only from one exceptional transaction.
Revenue remaining after every operating and financing cost has been deducted.
questions.explanation: Recurring describes repetition over time. The expression alone does not establish the payment date or turn revenue into a profit measure.

questions.q: A report says “revenue excludes the new subsidiary”, while a summary describes the figure as group-wide revenue. What should the summary preserve?
options: That the subsidiary’s sales are included because the summary uses a group heading.
The exclusion of the subsidiary from the reporting perimeter
That the omitted subsidiary necessarily had no activity during the period.
That the excluded sales can be treated as zero when describing the full group without further data.
questions.explanation: Une exclusion de périmètre doit rester explicite. Ne pas inclure une filiale dans un indicateur ne prouve ni l’absence de ventes de cette filiale ni un résultat consolidé.

questions.q: A manager translates “revenue generated by service contracts” as “trésorerie encaissée sur les contrats”. Which information has been added without support?
options: That contracts are relevant to the reported activity
That the sentence concerns the company’s business operations
That the recognised sales have already been collected in cash
That the business provides services rather than goods
questions.explanation: Generated revenue ne démontre pas un encaissement. La reformulation ajoute donc un statut de règlement que la phrase d’origine ne fournit pas.

questions.q: A financial note separately reports revenue, operating expenses and income tax. Which label identifies the tax on income rather than sales revenue?
options: Sales revenue
Operating revenue
Service revenue
Income tax
questions.explanation: Income tax désigne l’impôt sur le revenu ou le résultat selon le contexte. La présence de income ne doit pas le faire confondre avec les ventes.

questions.q: A company reports both “gross sales” and “sales net of discounts”. A summary uses the two figures interchangeably. What distinction should be restored?
options: Whether the sales figure is before or after the stated discounts
Whether the discounts affect the price billed or instead represent a change in the volume of units sold.
Whether both reported sales figures include the same discounts simply because both are described as revenue.
Whether the difference between gross and net sales can be treated as profit without considering other costs.
questions.explanation: Gross et net of discounts précisent ici la prise en compte des réductions. Un commentaire fidèle conserve le périmètre du montant utilisé sans mélanger les deux séries.

questions.q: A supplier issues a "credit note" to reduce part of an earlier invoice. Which description fits the document in this context?
options: A new invoice adding the same amount to the customer’s debt.
A document reducing the amount previously invoiced.
A bank loan agreement financing the customer’s purchase.
A reminder requesting immediate payment of the original invoice in full.
questions.explanation: The stated credit note adjusts the earlier invoice downwards. Credit in this document’s name does not mean a new bank loan or an additional charge.

questions.q: A customer pays an invoice that was already included in accounts receivable. Which description avoids recording the same sale twice?
options: Cash increases and the same invoice is recognised again as new revenue.
Cash increases while the same customer receivable remains fully outstanding.
Cash increases and the customer receivable is settled.
The receivable decreases while the customer payment is recorded as another expense.
questions.explanation: Le règlement solde une créance déjà constatée et apporte de la trésorerie. Il ne crée pas à lui seul une deuxième vente pour le même service.

questions.q: A report describes an invoice as “outstanding” and gives a due date next month. Which interpretation is accurate?
options: The invoice has been cancelled by the supplier.
The invoice has necessarily been paid in advance.
The invoice is necessarily overdue because it exists.
The invoice remains unpaid but is not yet overdue.
questions.explanation: Outstanding signifie ici non réglée. Une créance n’est overdue que si l’échéance est dépassée ; les deux termes ne sont pas automatiquement équivalents.

questions.q: A customer has not yet paid an invoice. A summary says “the receivable was collected”. What is wrong?
options: Collected incorrectly states that payment has been received.
Collected correctly states that the invoice remains unpaid.
Receivable means that the company owes the customer a loan.
An unpaid invoice cannot be described as a receivable.
questions.explanation: Collected annonce un encaissement réalisé. Si la facture reste impayée, on peut parler d’une créance outstanding, sans annoncer son règlement.

questions.q: The year-end receivables balance is higher than last year’s, but no sales or collection details are provided. Which statement is supported?
options: The increase measures the same increase in annual sales, without any need to examine settlements.
More customer amounts are outstanding at year-end.
The increase establishes a deterioration in overdue amounts even though no due dates are provided.
The increase measures the additional cash already received from the customers whose invoices remain outstanding.
questions.explanation: Le solde renseigne sur les créances non réglées à la clôture. À lui seul, il ne mesure ni les ventes de l’année ni les encaissements ni les retards de chaque client.

questions.q: An accountant asks for a "receivables ageing analysis" that groups unpaid customer invoices by how long they have been outstanding or overdue under the stated convention. What does the requested analysis classify?
options: The unpaid balances by customers’ credit limits, irrespective of the invoice dates.
The unpaid balances by invoice face value alone, without considering time outstanding.
The unpaid customer balances by their age under the specified convention.
The unpaid balances by billing currency alone, without considering due dates.
questions.explanation: Ageing concerns the time categories of the balances, not the age of customers’ businesses or employees. The reference convention must be understood when reading the categories.

questions.q: A customer sends a "remittance advice" identifying the invoices it says a transfer covers. Which description best fits this message?
options: A new invoice requesting an additional payment from the customer.
A statement that the supplier has cancelled every invoice mentioned.
A guarantee that the recipient’s bank has already credited the funds, independent of any bank check.
Information linking a stated payment to the invoices it is intended to settle.
questions.explanation: A remittance advice communicates payment allocation details. It is distinct from a new invoice or credit note and does not by itself replace checking whether funds have arrived.

questions.q: A company pays a supplier invoice whose expense was recorded last month. What does the payment do, without assuming any new purchase?
options: It settles the payable and reduces cash.
It settles the payable and records a second expense for the same purchase.
It reduces cash but leaves the same settled invoice fully outstanding in payables.
It increases cash while reducing the supplier payable, despite the company making the payment.
questions.explanation: Le paiement réduit la dette et la trésorerie. La charge ayant déjà été enregistrée, le règlement ne doit pas être présenté comme une nouvelle charge identique.

questions.q: An analyst translates “supplier payment terms” as “conditions d’encaissement des clients”. What relationship should the wording describe instead?
options: The conditions under which the company collects payment from its customers.
The conditions under which the company pays its suppliers
The discounts the company offers its customers for early settlement.
The terms under which the supplier pays the company’s outstanding customer invoices on its behalf.
questions.explanation: Supplier payment terms concerne le règlement des fournisseurs par l’entreprise. La traduction proposée inverse la relation en parlant de clients qui paient l’entreprise.

questions.q: A supplier extends an agreed invoice due date. No payment or cancellation occurs. Which description is accurate?
options: The payable is settled on the original due date solely because a later date was agreed.
The agreement on a later due date constitutes a payment received from the supplier.
The payable remains outstanding under a revised due date.
The change in due date alone is a cancellation of the remaining balance.
questions.explanation: Reporter l’échéance ne signifie ni régler ni annuler la dette. Le montant reste à payer selon la nouvelle date convenue.

questions.q: A note says “payables fell during the month”. A summary says “purchases fell by the same amount”. Why is that conclusion unsupported?
options: The decrease measures purchases net of sales, so payment timing need not be examined.
The closing supplier balance measures only new invoices received during the month.
A fall in the supplier balance can be attributed entirely to lower purchases without examining settlements.
The payable balance also depends on settlements, not only purchases.
questions.explanation: La variation des dettes dépend notamment des nouvelles factures et des règlements. Leur baisse ne permet pas d’isoler une baisse équivalente des achats.

questions.q: An accountant asks a supplier to confirm “the balance due to you”. From the company’s viewpoint, what is being checked?
options: The company’s payable to that supplier
The amount that the supplier owes the company, reversing the direction of the balance.
The company’s total purchases from that supplier, including invoices already settled.
The amount the company has already paid that supplier, rather than the balance still due.
questions.explanation: Due to you désigne une somme que l’entreprise doit au fournisseur destinataire. Le point de vue du rédacteur permet de choisir payable plutôt que receivable.

questions.q: A cash forecast describes a "shortfall" next month: available cash is below the payments due. What does shortfall refer to here?
options: The accounting loss necessarily reported for the whole financial year.
The gap between cash available and the cash needed for the payments.
The total value of all payments due, without deducting available cash.
The excess of available cash over the payments that need to be made.
questions.explanation: In this context a shortfall is an insufficiency relative to a funding need. It is not necessarily an accounting loss or the full payment amount.

questions.q: A cash-flow statement shows a payment for new equipment. Which fact should a summary report without assuming an immediate matching expense?
options: The equipment payment necessarily reduces current profit by its full amount at the payment date.
The equipment payment is a cash inflow because the asset value increased.
Cash was spent on an investment.
The payment can be reported as operating revenue merely because it supports future operations.
questions.explanation: L’achat payé constitue un flux de trésorerie d’investissement. Son effet sur les charges et le résultat n’est pas nécessairement identique au décaissement immédiat.

questions.q: A depreciation charge reduces accounting profit without a cash payment occurring at that moment. What does this illustrate?
options: The depreciation charge is a cash payment repeated on the date the original asset was bought.
The expense must be omitted from profit because there is no simultaneous cash payment.
The depreciation amount can be added to cash receipts as a new payment from a customer.
An accounting expense can differ from a current cash outflow.
questions.explanation: L’amortissement illustre une charge sans décaissement simultané. C’est une raison de distinguer le résultat comptable et les flux de trésorerie.

questions.q: A report refers specifically to “cash flow from operating activities”. Which scope should a translation retain?
options: Cash movements classified as operating activities
Cash from issuing shares and repaying loans, presented as if these were operating movements.
Cash from buying and selling long-term equipment, presented as the operating subtotal.
The closing cash balance at one date, presented as the period’s operating cash movement.
questions.explanation: Le complément from operating activities limite le périmètre aux activités opérationnelles. Le traduire par toute la trésorerie de l’entreprise élargirait silencieusement le champ.

questions.q: A summary treats a bank balance at one date as “cash flow during the year”. Which distinction has been lost?
options: An agreed budget versus an invoice payment deadline
A stock measured at a date versus movements measured over a period
A customer receipt versus a supplier payment in the same transaction
Gross revenue versus sales net of discounts
questions.explanation: Un solde bancaire est un stock à une date. Un cash flow décrit des mouvements sur une période ; les confondre modifie la nature de l’information financière.
